Berlin is expected to announce the planned move in the coming days, including "extensive" sanctions, three officials familiar with the matter told German newspaper Welt am Sonntag and the media outlet Politico. However, the three sources did not elaborate on what the specific measures could be. It is also unclear to what extent Berlin plans to hold Russia responsible for the Leipzig incident. On August 4, a drone loaded with explosives was discovered near Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig/Halle Airport, which serves as a hub for military aid shipments to Ukraine for its war against Russia . Merz told RTL in an interview on Thursday that the federal government would soon identify those responsible for the incident. https://p.dw.com/p/5JcLz Skip next section Sick leave now costs Germany twice as much as in 2010 08/29/2026 August 29, 2026 Sick leave now costs Germany twice as much as in 2010 The average number of sick days taken by German workers has risen sharply Image: Sergey Mironov/Zoonar/IMAGO The total amount of wages German firms paid in sick and maternity leave has more than doubled over the past 15 years, a study from the Cologne-based German Economic Institute (IW) shows. IW estimated that German companies paid a record-high €85.6 billion ($111 billion) in wages to employees who were out sick last year. This compares to €36.9 billion in 2010. Of the larger figure, €72.5 billion represented gross wages, while €13.1 billion was earmarked for social security contributions. IW said several factors have contributed to the rise, including wage hikes and inflation in other employee costs. The institute said the total number of employed people has also grown since 2010, meaning more workers are eligible for sick leave. IW, however, said it had noted a "significant" rise in recorded sick leave since Germany moved to electronic medical certificates in 2022. Separate research by the Berlin-based IGES Institute in January showed that German workers now take an average of 19.5 working days as sick leave per year, a noticeable increase from about 13 days in 2018. In an effort to stem the rise, Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government will from January ban patients from receiving sick notes from doctors by phone. Germany-US ties have soured since Trump's reelection, due to surprise tariffs, talk of seizing Greenland and open sniping over Russia's war in Ukraine and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war. https://p.dw.com/p/5Jc1M Skip next section Report: Taliban team in Berlin to aid Afghan deportations 08/29/2026 August 29, 2026 Report: Taliban team in Berlin to aid Afghan deportations There are three Afghan missions in Germany, located in Berlin, Bonn, and Munich [FILE: October 2024] Image: Friedrich Bungert/SZ Photo/picture alliance The Taliban has sent a team of three people to Germany to help facilitate the deportation of Afghan nationals, public broadcaster NDR reported. NDR said the delegation arrived in Germany on Wednesday and is staying at the Afghan embassy in Berlin. The broadcaster said their mission is to provide documents recognized by the Taliban in Kabul to Afghan nationals being deported from Germany. The delegation is also due to spend time in Bonn and Munich, where Afghanistan has consulates general. The arrival of the delegation is contentious as Germany — along with most of the rest of the world — does not recognize the Taliban government. Chancellor Friedrich Merz calls the contacts a purely technical necessity to return people with no right to stay. Critics, however, say his government is legitimizing the Taliban to help raise deportation numbers. Germany suspended deportations to Afghanistan when the Taliban returned to power in 2021. They resumed three years later, initially for convicted criminals. https://www.budapesttimes.hu/hungary/fro.text: The Budapest Times From forest fires to Paks: an army of all trades Soldiers prove themselves every day — the Minister of Defence highlighted this at the central celebration of the ministry and the Hungarian Defence Forces held on Wednesday in Budapest, at the Bálna Defence Centre, on the occasion of the national holiday. At the event marking the feast of the founding of the state and Saint Stephen, the founding king, Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi spoke about how the Hungarian Defence Forces prove themselves every day. As examples, he mentioned that without soldiers there would be no energy or nuclear security, that soldiers are building “the left bank” at Paks, that they ensure the water supply in the northern part of Budapest, that helicopters recently took part in extinguishing forest fires, and that many soldiers are serving abroad. “We draw on the past, but we must live in the present and continue on the path that is good for Hungary and the Hungarian Defence Forces,” said the minister. He added that what the future of the Hungarian Defence Forces will look like “really depends on us.” He believes the defence forces are “in very good hands” with Colonel General Zsolt Sándor, Chief of the Defence Staff, and that the task of the ministry is to provide the conditions necessary for its operation. He indicated that they have begun to deliver on the promises made during the election campaign. As examples, he mentioned that barracks and units are having their names restored, that the possibility has been created for those who were unjustly dismissed to return to the military, and that legislation is being prepared to provide the framework for further reforms. He also spoke about the fact that 2 percent of GDP can be allocated to the armed forces in accordance with NATO requirements, and that this money is spent on “what is truly good for the soldiers.” The minister stressed that those being recognised set an example for everyone, and that work done always bears fruit. At the event, resolutions on appointments and promotions were presented, and decorations and awards were presented by the defence minister and General Zsolt Sándor, Chief of the General Staff of the Hungarian Defence Forces. The Hazai Samu Lifetime Achievement Award, bestowed by the minister, was presented to retired General Zoltán Szenes in recognition of his exemplary military career and the outstandingly significant theoretical and practical work he carried out in the course of that career in support of the fulfilment of the defence forces’ tasks. https://www.politico.eu/article/uk-vows-.text: LONDON — Britain's top finance minister on Wednesday promised an uplift in defense spending by 2030 to "set the direction" for meeting a crucial NATO target — but didn't lay out how the government will get there. John Healey quit as U.K. defense secretary in the dying days of Keir Starmer's government in a row over funding. On Wednesday he gave his first budget as chancellor under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, setting out the government's tax and spending plans. Healey committed for the first time to spending 3% of GDP on the nation's defenses by 2030 — something he had called for when he quit Starmer's administration. But he declined to say where he would find the money, a staging post on the way to meeting NATO's target of 3.5% of GDP by 2035. Instead, he said a broader review of government spending would address it next year. Advertisement Advertisement Increasing spending would include "looking hard at public spending" and using "innovative financing," including a joint procurement initiative with Finland, Poland, and the Netherlands, Healey vowed. Healey's more immediate task was to find £4.7 billion to plug gaps in the blueprint for developing the U.K.'s armed forces, the Defence Investment Plan , published earlier this year after long delays. The Treasury said £3 billion would come from "reprioritization of capital budgets" across the U.K. government, including £1.7 billion of cuts to the energy department. The chancellor and prime minister both sought to show they had prioritized the U.K.'s security commitments in the budget, with Burnham and Healey speaking to Volodymyr Zelenskyy ahead of the statement and pledging £10 billion in additional economic and military support for Ukraine. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte posted on X : "I welcome this move to put [the U.K.] on a credible path towards meeting the commitment made by all NATO Allies in The Hague — to ensure we’re all investing what’s needed to remain ready [and] able to deter aggression and defend our freedom and security." However, the lack of detail did not go unnoticed in the budget's immediate aftermath. Conservative Party Leader Kemi Badenoch responded to Healey's speech: "You can't have social security without national security... There are huge problems coming down the road but this Budget is simply trying to get through the day." Kelly Maddison of the manufacturers' body Make UK Defence said work is needed "on how exactly it plans to reach 3% of GDP on defence by 2030" and "industry needs to know that the commitment to defence is there long term to strengthen business confidence to invest.” Advertisement Advertisement
